chunks: A man stayed as a guest with ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام for some days, then he brought before him a legal dispute which he had not mentioned to ʿAlī عليه السلام.
So ʿAlī عليه السلام said to him, “Are you a litigant?” He said, “Yes.”
He said, “Move away from us, for the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم forbade that a litigant be hosted unless his opponent is with him.”

key_terms.تَحَوَّلْ: move away or withdraw from this lodging
key_terms.حُكُومَةٍ: a legal dispute or case brought for judgment
key_terms.خَصْمٌ: a litigant or disputing party in a case
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose ruling is being cited

ai.seo_question: Can a judge host one litigant in a dispute before hearing the case?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches judicial impartiality and proper etiquette in adjudication. Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام refused to continue hosting a man once it became clear that he was a litigant in a case, acting upon the prohibition of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم against showing one-sided hospitality to a disputant apart from his opponent.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3236 - A man stayed as a guest with Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) for a few days. Then he presented a legal dispute to him, which he had not previously mentioned to Imam Ali (as).

So Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said to him: "Are you a litigant?"
He replied: "Yes."
Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) said: "Then leave us, for the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) forbade hosting a litigant except when his opponent is also present."
